name: Riliprubart
summary: Riliprubart is Sanofi's wholly owned anti-C1s (classical complement) monoclonal antibody for chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP). MOBILIZE (NCT06290128, SOC-refractory CIDP) was stopped for futility on 2026-06-10, so only VITALIZE is modelled: NCT06290141, about 160 adults on IVIg maintenance randomised 1:1 to riliprubart or IVIg, primary completion 2027-07-09, with Sanofi guiding phase 3 data and a US/EU submission in 2027. Price anchor: Vyvgart Hytrulo, the only non-immunoglobulin biologic labelled for CIDP, at its 2024 CMS Part B spend per beneficiary ($167,216), less the Part B ASP gap. Uptake anchor: Vyvgart Hytrulo's measured CIDP launch rate (1,316 patients in the 224 days to 2025-01-31, 2.78% of the US CIDP pool a year) at a 1.0 multiple, applied to the IVIg-treated quarter of the pool (Gable 2026: 20,367 of 77,058 had an IVIG claim in 2023; second reader corrected from Blein's 32.65% chronic share, which overran the pool's own immunoglobulin count).

therapy_mode.source: NCT06290141 (clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06290141): riliprubart is tested as maintenance therapy against maintenance IVIg, 24 weeks blinded then 24 weeks open label; Neurology 2025 trial-design abstract (doi.org/10.1212/WNL.0000000000208529)
therapy_mode.note: Maintenance of a chronic autoimmune neuropathy, continued indefinitely like the IVIg it would replace
therapy_mode.check: Sanofi Q2 2026 6-K 0001628280-26-050803 exhibit 2 and 6-K 0001121404-26-000008 (read in book filing_sections): VITALIZE (NCT06290141) enrols IVIg-treated CIDP patients and continues as planned; book trials row: randomised, quadruple-masked, riliprubart vs IVIg, 160 enrolled, start 2024-08-21. Web (rarediseaseadvisor.com, 'New Study to Compare Riliprubart and IVIG in CIDP'): patients on IVIg maintenance, 24 weeks blinded then 24 weeks open label. Maintenance of a chronic disease, so chronic holds.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand 'Vyvgart Hytrulo': CMS Part B 2024, $150,829,226 over 902 beneficiaries = $167,216
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Vyvgart Hytrulo (efgartigimod/hyaluronidase) is the only non-immunoglobulin biologic approved for CIDP in the US (June 2024) and the product a new CIDP biologic would be priced against. Case against: (1) CMS 2024 beneficiaries mix gMG and CIDP and include partial-year CIDP starts from a June 2024 launch, so $167,216 understates a full year (Part D 2024 was $191,644, Vyvgart IV Part B 2024 $231,053); (2) VITALIZE's comparator is IVIg itself, which the book carries no CIDP-labelled brand for (only Octagam, labelled for other uses), and chronic IVIg can cost less than an FcRn blocker. Riliprubart's route of administration in phase 3 was not confirmed in this research; Part B is assumed because the trial compares against infused IVIg
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand 'Vyvgart': Vyvgart Hytrulo Part B 2024 $150,829,226 / 902 beneficiaries = $167,216.44, so 0.167216 mm USD. Part D 2024 $191,644 and Vyvgart IV Part B 2024 $231,053 also match the note. Unit right (mm USD per patient-year). Comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its case against. Route, which the researcher left open: web search (rarediseaseadvisor.com; withpower.com trial listing) says VITALIZE gives riliprubart by IV or subcutaneous injection and describes riliprubart as weekly subcutaneous, so a Part B / Part D split like Hytrulo's (902 B, 658 D) is plausible; the Part B anchor stays a judgement.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of ASP, and ASP is net of manufacturer discounts and rebates; 1 - 1/1.06 = 5.66%. Same rule as the book's frexalimab seed (lookup.py seed Frexalimab)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: net is 94.3% of the CMS figure. Case against: if riliprubart is dispensed subcutaneously through Part D and commercial pharmacy benefits, the house 0.5 applies instead; Vyvgart Hytrulo is itself split between Part B (902) and Part D (658) beneficiaries in 2024
gross_to_net_pct.check: 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.0566; same value and rule as the book's frexalimab seed (lookup.py seed Frexalimab). Direction right: share off, net = 94.34% of $167,216 = $157,751. Consistent with the price anchor, because a Part B per-beneficiary figure is ASP-based and already net of rebates. The note's case against is now live: VITALIZE doses riliprubart IV or subcutaneously (weekly SC per rarediseaseadvisor.com), so part of use may fall under Part D, where the house 0.5 applies to a gross Part D anchor instead. Hytrulo's own Part D gross ($191,644) sits only 18% above its Part B ASP-based net, which argues against 0.5 for this class.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the stock per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Anderson-Smits C, ..., Layton JB, Neurology and Therapy 2023 (PubMed 37171778, doi.org/10.1007/s40120-023-00478-5), MarketScan 2008-2018, 3,975 CIDP IVIg initiators: of the 68% who reached a steady-state maintenance dose, 27% discontinued their index IVIg by year 1 and a further 6% switched immunoglobulin
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement: this is IVIg's measured maintenance persistence, the population VITALIZE enrols, used as the proxy because no persistence figure for a CIDP biologic was found (ADHERE+ reports near-complete rollover and a mean 58 weeks on drug, PubMed 42463457, but no annual stop rate). Case against: adding the 6% who switched gives 0.33; a new mechanism after MOBILIZE's futility in refractory patients may see more early stopping for lack of effect
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 37171778 (doi 10.1007/s40120-023-00478-5) full text: 3,975 CIDP IVIG initiators, MarketScan 2008-2018, Sankey from the steady-state dose at 4-month intervals. The 68% / 27% / 6% figures sit in the Sankey figure, not the PMC body text; a web search of the paper (RTI Health Solutions PDF, pubmed) returned 'Most (68%) patients arrived at steady-state dose with index IVIG treatment; of those, 27% discontinued the index IVIG and 6% switched immunoglobulin treatment by year 1'. The citation is fixed: the first author is Anderson-Smits and Layton is the last author (Layton is first author of the companion paper, PMID 37195408). The value is unchanged. Case for higher, not in the note: the whole cohort's index-IVIG discontinuation rate was 107.95 per 100 person-years, but that includes loading-phase non-responders, not the maintenance population VITALIZE enrols. ADHERE+ (PMID 42463457): 228/229 rolled over, mean 58.0 weeks on drug, matches the note.

forecast_start_year.source: Brief convention: the first full year after 2026
forecast_start_year.note: Expected launch is later. VITALIZE primary completion 2027-07-09 (NCT06290141); Sanofi's milestone table lists 'riliprubart CIDP phase 3 data, regulatory submission (US, EU)' in 2027 (Sanofi Q2 2026 results press release, 6-K 0001121404-26-000008). A late-2027 BLA with a standard 12-month review gives a late-2028 approval and 2029 as the first full year; the ramp midpoint carries that shift
forecast_start_year.check: Brief convention 2027. VITALIZE primary completion 2027-07-09 (context file and book trials row, last update 2026-09-22). Sanofi Q2 2026 press release 6-K 0001121404-26-000008 (book filing_sections) lists, under 2027, 'riliprubart CIDP phase 3 data, regulatory submission (US, EU)'. A 2029 first full year is consistent with a standard review.

exus_multiple.source: argenx FY2025 results (argenx.com/news/2026/press-release-3245199; 20-F 0001697862-26-000032): Vyvgart franchise product net sales US $3,533.9mm, Japan $206.8mm, China $67.9mm, rest of world $342.6mm; 617.3 / 3,533.9 = 0.1747
exus_multiple.note: Judgement: the closest marketed CIDP biologic's filed split, though it blends gMG with CIDP and argenx is a younger commercial organisation outside the US than Sanofi. Case for higher: Sanofi's own Dupixent ran 0.36 ex-US per US in 2025 (book asset_revenue_regions: EU 1,957 + ROW 2,219 over US 11,538), and IVIg is rationed in Europe, which could favour a non-plasma product there
exus_multiple.check: Web search of argenx's 2025 annual report / 20-F (sec.gov 000169786226000032, matches the cited accession 0001697862-26-000032): product net sales US $3,533.9mm, Japan $206.8mm, China $67.9mm, rest of world $342.6mm. (206.8+67.9+342.6)/3,533.9 = 617.3/3,533.9 = 0.1747. Book asset_revenue_regions Dupixent 2025: (1,957+2,219)/11,538 = 0.362, as the note says. China is argenx's product sales under its Zai Lab licence, which understates end-market China. Labelled judgement.

economics_share.source: Sanofi half-year financial report 2026, 6-K 0001628280-26-050803 exhibit 99.2: the R&D pipeline appendix lists 'riliprubart C1s mAb IVIg-treated CIDP' with no collaboration footnote (footnotes cover only Regeneron, Teva, ImmuNext, SK bioscience); the book's asset_economics table holds no partner row
economics_share.check: Book filing_sections, 6-K 0001628280-26-050803 exhibit 2 pipeline appendix: 'riliprubart C1s mAb IVIg-treated CIDP' with no collaboration marker; the collaboration footnotes are (a) Regeneron, (b) Teva, (c) ImmuNext, (d) SK bioscience. Book asset_economics has no row for asset 3089 (Riliprubart). Wholly owned, 1.0.

prevalence.source: Gable et al., Neuroepidemiology 2026 (PubMed 41525422, doi.org/10.1159/000550418): Inovalon claims, adjusted 2023 prevalence 23.3 per 100,000, an estimated 77,058 people with CIDP in the US
prevalence.note: lookup.py pool returned nothing for CIDP or this indication name, and data/epidemiology.csv has no CIDP row, so this asset carries the pool. Claims-based, and the authors flag possible misclassification of CIDP codes, which would overstate it; older estimates are far lower (roughly 3 to 9 per 100,000). Authors are Roivant/Immunovant-affiliated
prevalence.check: PubMed 41525422 full text (PMC12880827): adjusted prevalence 23.3 per 100,000 persons, an estimated 77,058 individuals living with CIDP in the USA in 2023. Funded by Immunovant, with Roivant/Immunovant authors, as the note says. lookup.py pool for 'Polyradiculo', 'CIDP' and 'Demyelinating' returns nothing, and data/epidemiology.csv has no CIDP row, so the asset carries the pool.

incidence.source: Same source: adjusted 2023 incidence 2.8 per 100,000, about 9,238 new cases
incidence.check: PubMed 41525422 full text: adjusted incidence 2.8 per 100,000 (95% CI 2.7-2.9), 'approximately 9,238 patients diagnosed with CIDP in 2023'.

eligible_pct.source: Gable et al., Neuroepidemiology 2026 (PubMed 41525422, doi.org/10.1159/000550418), Table 2, the same source and year as the pool: of the 77,058 extrapolated prevalent US CIDP patients, 20,367 had at least one IVIG claim in 2023. 20,367 / 77,058 = 26.43%
eligible_pct.note: Judgement kept from the researcher: the label is assumed to follow VITALIZE's IVIg-treated population (Sanofi's pipeline names the indication 'IVIg-treated CIDP', 6-K 0001628280-26-050803) now that MOBILIZE has stopped. Taken from the pool's own source because Blein's 1,113/3,409 chronic share (Komodo, 81% of the cohort treated) applied to Gable's pool (53.9% treated) gives 25,159, which is more than every patient on any immunoglobulin in Gable's 2023 pool (21,538). 77,058 x 0.2643 = 20,367 patients. Case for lower: this counts any IVIG claim in the year, and chronic users (8 or more courses) were only 1,113 of 1,803 immunoglobulin users in Blein 2026 (PubMed 41696747), so 0.2643 x 0.6173 = 0.163 on a cross-source basis. Case for higher: adding subcutaneous immunoglobulin gives 21,538 / 77,058 = 0.2795, and an FDA label could read 'CIDP' broadly.
eligible_pct.check: Blein 2026 (PubMed 41696747) abstract confirms 1,113 chronic Ig users of 3,409 (32.65%) and 1,803 Ig users (52.9%), but the ratio does not transfer to the Gable pool. Gable's full text (PMC12880827) Table 2, prevalent cohort n = 77,058: 41,505 treated in 2023 (53.9%), immunoglobulin 21,538, IVIG 20,367, SCIG 1,496. The researcher's 0.3265 x 77,058 = 25,159 IVIg-maintained patients exceeds Gable's 21,538 on any immunoglobulin. Corrected 0.3265 -> 0.2643 (20,367 / 77,058) from the pool's own source.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool captured per year at peak
penetration_peak_pct.source: argenx AAN 2025 release (argenx.com/news/2024/argenx-highlights-vyvgart-data-at-aan-2025-setting-new-standard): 1,316 CIDP patients treated with Vyvgart Hytrulo as of 2025-01-31, 224 days after the 2024-06-21 FDA approval. Annualised 1,316 x 365/224 = 2,144 a year, over the 77,058 CIDP pool (Gable 2026) = 2.78%
penetration_peak_pct.note: 1.0 multiple, a judgement. The incumbent's rate is taken over its own label pool (all CIDP) and applied to riliprubart's narrower one, giving about 700 new starts a year at peak. Case for higher: launch-period rates understate peak, and IVIg-maintained patients are the group most actively switched (AAN 2026: 91 of 225 surveyed Hytrulo patients had attempted an IVIg switch). Case for lower: riliprubart would be a second novel mechanism behind an established FcRn blocker, with a failed refractory-population trial on record. CMS beneficiaries were not used because Hytrulo's mix gMG and CIDP
penetration_peak_pct.check: Web search (argenx.com/news/2024/argenx-highlights-vyvgart-data-at-aan-2025-setting-new-standard; GlobeNewswire 2025-04-08): 'as of January 31, 2025, real-world data for 1,316 CIDP patients treated with VYVGART Hytrulo'. 2024-06-21 to 2025-01-31 = 224 days. 1,316 x 365/224 = 2,144.4 a year; / 77,058 = 2.783%. The arithmetic holds. Caveat: the release does not say US only, and Japan and China had CIDP approvals by late 2024, so a small ex-US share may be included. The 1.0 multiple is labelled with cases both ways. After the eligible correction: 0.0278 x 20,367 = 566 new starts a year at peak (the researcher had about 700).

ramp_steepness.source: Reused from the book's fenebrutinib seed (lookup.py seed Fenebrutinib): fitted to Kesimpta's six-point measured new-start series 2020-2025, k 0.626
ramp_steepness.note: Judgement: no measured CIDP launch curve exists in the book (Vyvgart Hytrulo has one CMS year). Kesimpta is a specialist-prescribed immunology biologic launched into an established market, the nearest measured analogue. Case against: rare-disease launches through a concentrated neuromuscular prescriber base usually ramp faster
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py seed Fenebrutinib: ramp_steepness 0.63, 'fitted with the midpoint above to Kesimpta's six-point new-start series' (k 0.626). The reuse is a labelled judgement.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Kesimpta-fitted midpoint of 3.078 years after launch (lookup.py seed Fenebrutinib) plus 2 years for a 2029 first full year against the 2027 forecast start
ramp_midpoint_year.note: The 2029 first full year is inferred from VITALIZE primary completion (2027-07-09) and Sanofi's 2027 submission guidance (Sanofi Q2 2026 results press release, 6-K 0001121404-26-000008), assuming a standard review; not announced
ramp_midpoint_year.check: lookup.py seed Fenebrutinib: midpoint 3.078 years after launch, and that seed adds 1 year for a 2028 first full year against 2027. Here 3.078 + 2 = 5.078, rounded to 5.08, for a 2029 first full year: primary completion 2027-07-09 (book trials row) plus Sanofi's 2027 data and submission guidance (6-K 0001121404-26-000008, read in the book) plus a standard review. The 2029 year is inferred, not announced, as the note says.
